summary: This release uses stock OMP v18.12.5 as its engineering baseline. The 28 changelog entries below record the changes since v0.7.7. Historical receipts do not qualify these bytes.
highlights:
- This release uses stock OMP v18.12.5 as its engineering baseline. The 28 changelog entries below record the changes since v0.7.7. Historical receipts do not qualify these bytes.
- Advisory Percy visual review of 18 deterministic, authored synthetic states across phone, 810×1080 tablet and desktop CSS viewports, with fail-closed serialized DOM/resource canary guards and source/serialized layout parity. CI always validates locally and uploads only for same-repository PRs, main pushes and GitHub-hosted dispatches; forks and gateway-ci dispatches receive no Percy secret. No production source or runtime assets change.
- BrowserStack setup/baseline/renewal runbook and ADR-035 separating Percy visual review, TestingBot release deviceCloud, Automate fallback under ADR-032, and capability-free manual Live review. Sponsorship review is due 2027-09-20 before the 2027-10-20 expiry.
- Add BrowserStack Automate Mobile as an immediate pre-write fallback for empty TestingBot iPad and Samsung Android pools, keeping iPhone/Home Screen Push TestingBot-only and targets sequential. Pin Local 8.9 under Rosetta with the documented single-user child-argv exception, shared CONNECT containment, private crash-cleaned config, vendor-qualified ownership, per-target release attribution, complete retained-record audits and verified record deletion. Persist signed artifact inventories only in private recovery progress, require every artifact absent before restoration, and re-audit crash cleanup or count unaudited deletions explicitly. Detect opaque failed-command media and canonicalize Local ownership through symlinked paths. Accept references only as whole HTTP(S) string values with one scheme/hostname occurrence and no comma; reject reference-like keys or other values, retaining the exact dashboard exemption. Require each pinned hostname's raw and canonical JSON census to equal accepted reference counts. Extend that census to bounded fixpoint percent-decoded text and a single decoded scheme per reference, with character-class-pinned dashboard paths/queries and no userinfo, ports or fragments. Persist an incident for any unbound pre-build reference instead of retaining volatile pending references; deletion/absence checks still proceed, but fresh cleanup cannot clear the incident. Atomically checkpoint post-audit artifact references with an incident while continuing only deletion/absence verification across crashes, and reject data/media keys using value classification. Keep DELETE and bounded absence checks running after post-audit validation failures by atomically recording an unvalidated-record incident and safely recovered strict-JSON whole-value references. Verify record/log absence before failing for missing inventory, and accept clean XML/text artifact 404 or reviewed media-403 bodies after raw scans/censuses without falsely requiring JSON. Scan every non-media retained-surface body before rejection, whatever its status, including pre/post-audit errors and transient GET-retry bodies, and persist capability hits as incidents. Preserve monotonic cleanup stages and recovery dependencies on release failure. Identify retitled Local descendants by PID/birth lineage, not argv; prepare before owning a tunnel. Keep signed-log expiry limits explicit and refuse the fallback entitlement from 2027-10-20 without a reviewed renewal. Public-page development probes do not qualify a release.
- Add explicit same-receipt device-cloud availability resumption: finish publication lifecycle before reporting a clean hold, preserve other passed qualification proof, and require one guarded operator authorization per immutable release-driver retry job. Infrastructure holds never pass qualification, auto-retry, or clear ordinary failures or foreign host ownership. Keep machine outcomes in atomic private per-phase files rather than noisy lane stdout, record every hold leaf, consume old resume eligibility before setup, bind both hold scopes to the immutable worker host/source/policy, and replay a failed unclaimed tmux launch in the same job.
- Widen TestingBot's modern iPhone and Samsung device pools with explicit OS floors and canonical Galaxy hardware checks; keep A55 disabled pending an observed hardware-code proof. Check free inventory during read-only preflight and distinguish typed availability holds (exit 75) from diagnostic failures without changing schema 3 or qualification claims. Audit every partial attempt for exact contiguous 16-character link windows, minimize vendor-logged page results, attest before opening capabilities, and stage the cloud fixture only under the Pixel lease. Keep targets sequential within the vendor's session limit, block queued Pixel lanes after any release failure, and audit raw plus canonical retained metadata, asset inventories and declared logs. A shared strict JSON parser rejects duplicate keys at every depth before discovering references, with a parse-site invariant against lenient bypasses. Application asset checks return only an in-page comparison boolean to vendor command logs.
- Move the OMP engineering baseline to published v18.12.5 (#423), with pins derived by `scripts/upstream-pins.ts`. Registry v1, the discovery file format and socket paths, the relay protocol, `collab.autoStart`, `packages/wire/src/index.ts`, and every collaboration and `collab-web` source are unchanged from v18.12.3. Within the tracked paths, only `docs/extensions.md` documents GitLab MR references for `ctx.annotations` (can1357/oh-my-pi#16361) and the version bumps touch `package.json`; neither changes what the gateway reads or sends. The embedded client remains at v18.4.2. No qualification is claimed; published v0.7.7 stays bound to OMP v18.10.2.
- Move the OMP engineering baseline to published v18.12.3 (#409), with pins derived by `scripts/upstream-pins.ts`. Registry v1, the discovery file format and socket paths, the relay protocol, `collab.autoStart`, and the collaboration `host.ts`, `registry.ts`, `settings.ts`, and `packages/wire/src/index.ts` sources are unchanged from v18.10.2. Session entries gain an optional `runtime` build identity (can1357/oh-my-pi#15680), a CLI guest's prompt-cache key changes (can1357/oh-my-pi#15467), and the `collab-web` eval renderer changes (can1357/oh-my-pi#12730); none changes what the gateway reads or sends. The embedded client remains at v18.4.2. No qualification is claimed; published v0.7.7 stays bound to OMP v18.10.2.
- Rewrite the README, public site home page, and operator and user documentation reader-first. The README leads with the product promise, demo, a three-step quickstart, everyday use, the privacy model, and a two-column supported-platforms table, and drops release-ledger prose, fork-era history, and the architecture diagram. New `docs/README.md` indexes every document by task (use, trust, build on, dated records) and new `docs/USAGE.md` explains the directory, View and Control, Needs you, hold and hide, background alerts, app installation, and error states from the phone holder's point of view. `docs/OPERATIONS.md` keeps its numbered headings but reads as a task guide with a configuration table, doctor check list, and troubleshooting-by-symptom table; installer transaction internals move to `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. `docs/UPGRADE_ROLLBACK.md` opens with upgrade, rollback, boundary recovery, and what rollback never does, and restores the v0.6.0–v0.7.0 predecessor sections the release ledger links. `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` leads with the support table and a plain current claim. Stale current-state claims (v0.4.0 status, Windows and background Web Push "not yet qualified", the ADR-018 worker-navigation gap) are corrected across the root security policy, package READMEs, and runbook introductions; the site home page, `llms.txt`, and all four site pages gain a Docs link. `scripts/docs-links.test.ts` fails on any relative Markdown link or heading fragment that does not resolve.
- Visual QA of the README on GitHub's desktop and phone renders: the install step is now one copyable block (`tar`, `cd`, `install`, `serve-guidance`, shared with Operations) instead of archive names in prose; the supported-platforms table shows the qualified OMP commit as a short SHA linked to the exact upstream commit so the table no longer scrolls sideways on a phone; the settings-sheet capture appears once, beside the background-alerts bullet. `release-generate` approve emits the linked short commit.
- The README adds BrowserStack's open-source attribution ("This project is tested with BrowserStack") below the TestingBot real-device acknowledgement.
- Retain the Linux qualification droplet's create id before waiting for its public IPv4. Null networks and parse/API errors no longer mean resource absence; teardown deletes the bound id, requires HTTP 204/404 and fails if billing remains. Preserve credential-free provider response bodies and statuses as workflow artifacts, including failed cleanup.
- Allow up to 180 seconds for each authenticated WinRM probe on a fresh Windows qualification instance, still capped by the shared 12-minute allocation/admission deadline and requiring three consecutive successes spanning at least 60 seconds. Retain credential-free per-probe start, first-response, signal and exit timing in Windows progress and evidence, including failed admission and cleanup, without changing qualification pass gates.
- Fail closed on classified Percy diagnostics from either output stream and refuse snapshot POSTs after an SDK warning. Upload mode now audits the exact redacted CLI-log candidate after an isolated 18-state testing-host run and proves a planted SDK-log canary is rejected. Document that Percy uploads CLI logs with every build; the opt-out disables CI logs only.
- Run the Percy CLI under native Node instead of Bun's incompatible HTTP server layer, and pin its CI Node 24.22.0 LTS runtime. Preserve sanitized phase/reason/count diagnostics through both runner layers so a created build with zero accepted snapshots cannot hide its failing boundary.
- Disable automatic Percy drop-in baseline seeding; baseline approval stays manual. Classify CLI diagnostics without exposing their text. Only CLI 1.32.11's exact unconditional future-Node startup notice is nonfatal on the already-pinned Node 24 runtime; SDK/unknown warnings stay fatal.
- Resolve Percy Node executables through the platform-native lookup (including Windows), and disable test-only CSS animation replay so source/serialized parity does not capture entrance motion.
- Poll for the installed WebAPK's DevTools page target before judging the published-byte smoke render, with a fail-closed deadline and sanitized timeout diagnostics.
- Open sessions on tablet and desktop widths are no longer squeezed into the directory's 35rem column (#411, #412). The directory's `main` rule also sized the embedded client's `<main>`, so the transcript stayed 542px wide and code lines showed about 45 characters. From 37rem up, the session, its header, and its triage bar share one centered `min(100% − 2rem, 60rem)` column, and the transcript reaches the client's own 900px width (about 88 characters per code line). The directory keeps its 35rem triage column, and nothing changes below 37rem.
- The embedded-ask browser test now waits out the relay client's backoff after the relay returns. Its 5-second wait failed on slow runners, because each held reconnect doubles the retry delay to as much as 15 seconds under the test's fixed jitter.
- The deviceCloud lane reads TestingBot's iPhone session start correctly. TestingBot answers with a W3C `value` and also echoes the session id at the top level. The lane took that wrapper for the capabilities, so it refused every such allocation as "another platform or browser". This was found by the first Studio development run. Session start now reads the W3C `value`, still accepts JSON Wire responses, and treats two different session ids as an unidentified create.
- The iPhone Home Screen install now expands Safari's shortened share sheet on every observed iOS 26 release. The expansion cell is labelled "View More" on 26.4 but "More" on 26.2, so the second development run could not find Add to Home Screen on an iPhone Air. The lane taps only that cell, never Safari's toolbar More button, which dismisses the sheet. Each install step now waits for the element it needs instead of a fixed pause, because an iPhone 17 Pro Max that had passed four times once rendered its menu's Share action later than the former 1.5-second pause.
- Pin the BrowserStack `browser_url`, `public_url`, `logs`, `video_url` and insight `optimize_url` shapes found by the third Studio development run, keeping dashboard/docs hosts unfetched and retaining only fixed audit/parser causes in memory while progress and receipts remain generic.
- Resolve the BrowserStack contracts exposed by Studio development runs four and five: accept the observed S26 `SM-S942U1`, ignore non-media capability echoes, track re-signed logs by object identity with the latest persisted URL, diagnose installed-shell timeouts with closed codes, and distinguish completed incident removals from unverified removal.
- The local Percy health test allows 30 seconds, the portable lane's per-test default. On a cold Windows runner, starting Node and loading `@percy/core` took longer than its former 10-second limit.
- Close the PR #421 review gaps: detect nested/raw image retention without treating capability echoes as media, persist every failed BrowserStack audit through deletion/crash recovery, reject conflicting WebDriver ids regardless of capabilities shape, and permit only complete six-key signed-artifact queries plus optional `response-content-type`.
- Require the pinned session-bound BrowserStack `video_url` presentation on finalized records, and detect text-log media under unquoted/single/double-quoted keys and `:`/`=` assignments without treating quoted placeholders as retained containers.
- Preserve running-session media incidents across clean finalization and detect binary image/video signatures in non-media-labelled retained bodies before decoding, retaining the existing bounds, decoded text scans and declared-media body cancellations.
- Refuse BrowserStack retained text in any encoding other than UTF-8. A declared non-UTF-8 or repeated charset, or a decoded NUL (UTF-16/32 without a byte-order mark), is an incident, so interleaved text cannot hide a capability window from the scan.

stableRollback: The selected predecessor is v0.7.7. Gateway rollback does not switch or restart the separately running OMP process. This release uses stock OMP v18.12.5. rollback --to selects only retained runtimes. Preserve configuration and readiness-token state; see docs/UPGRADE_ROLLBACK.md for predecessor compatibility and stopped-service recovery.

plannedBoundary: - Planned qualification: Debian 13 x86-64; macOS 27.0 (26A428) arm64 in a Virtualization.framework guest (VirtualMac2,1, ADR-033); a disposable Windows Server 2025 host (the Administrator lifecycle and a fresh standard-user install); Chrome on the physical Pixel 10 Pro, including its background-Push lane; and real iPhone, iPad, and Galaxy devices in TestingBot's cloud. Every lane must pass against these exact signed bytes before stable promotion; the plan is not evidence.
candidateRollback: The selected predecessor is v0.7.7; pruning keeps it installed as the recorded rollback target. Gateway rollback does not switch or restart OMP. Historical fork-era recovery is documented separately in docs/UPGRADE_ROLLBACK.md.
